_README: Shared fixtures for the server/client URL-decision differential test.
Read by BOTH internal/server/urlvalidate_differential_test.go (which asserts
the "server" column against validateURLField) and web/src/util/safe-url.test.ts
(which asserts the "client" column against safeHref). Neither side can drift
without turning its own test red, and a case can only be silenced by editing
this file, which shows up in review.
This file exists because safe-url.ts used to claim the two guards agreed, so
that "a scheme the client allows and the server rejects is unreachable". The
SCHEME SETS agree. The DECISIONS do not: 9 of these 42 inputs are decided
differently. Every divergence is recorded below with a measured reason.
PINNED AND SAMPLED -- NOT BOUNDED. An earlier version of this README said the
disagreement was "pinned and bounded", and the word mattered: it invites a
reader to treat these 9 as the whole set. An independent audit ran 39 further
inputs through both validators and found 10 MORE divergent shapes outside this
file, among them http:\\evil.com, https:/\evil.com, http:\/\/evil.com,
http://example.com\@evil.com/, https://ex%41mple.com/ (percent-encoded host:
net/url errors, WHATWG decodes to example.com), https:example.com/x,
https:/example.com/x, https:////x, https://///x and https://example.com:65536/x.
So at least 19 shapes are known to diverge and this file pins 9 of them. The
set is NOT closed. All 19 resolve to http(s) or are inert, which is the useful
result -- finding a new divergent shape is not by itself evidence that
something broke, and adding it here as a pin is welcome.
SECURITY READING: none of the 9 is a scheme escalation. In every case where
the client is the more permissive of the two, the input resolves to an http(s)
URL -- an attacker-chosen HOST, which is already reachable through a plainly
accepted https://evil.com/, and not an attacker-chosen SCHEME. They are
broken-link and inconsistency bugs, not XSS. Do not delete a case because it
looks harmless; the point is that the disagreement is pinned and its measured
reason recorded next to it.
BASE-DEPENDENCE. safeHref decides on new URL(raw) with NO base. The sink is an
<a> in a document, which ALWAYS resolves against the document base, and under
WHATWG rules an input whose scheme equals the base's scheme is parsed as a
RELATIVE reference. So for some inputs the host safeHref reasoned about is not
the host the browser will navigate to. "base_dependent": true marks every case
whose resolved host differs between an http dashboard and an https one. It is
measured at a real JSDOM anchor by testBaseDependenceMarkersAreAccurate() in
safe-url.test.ts, which fails if a marker is added or omitted wrongly -- so the
marker is a checked fact, not an annotation. Do not quote a host out of a note
as the host the browser will use unless the case is unmarked. This is a
correctness-of-documentation issue only: the base is always http(s), so a
base-relative resolution can never escalate the SCHEME.
"accept" for the server means validateURLField returns nil. "accept" for the
client means safeHref returns the input unchanged.

cases.name: empty
cases.note: Server is MORE permissive: validateURLField treats "" as "unset" so a caller can clear the field, while on the client new URL("") throws and safeHref renders no link. Same user-visible outcome, different vocabulary. BASE-DEPENDENT: an empty href resolves to the document itself, so at the sink the host is the dashboard's own and no host of the input is involved at all.

cases.name: backslash host confusion
cases.note: Client is MORE permissive: WHATWG reads the backslashes as slashes, so new URL() yields host "evil.com" and the browser navigates there; net/url yields Host == "" and the server's host check rejects it. Not base-dependent -- measured "evil.com" under both an http and an https document base.

cases.name: single slash host
cases.note: Client is MORE permissive: WHATWG normalises new URL("http:/example.com") to host "example.com"; net/url treats it as an opaque/rootless path with Host == "". BASE-DEPENDENT: "example.com" is the base-less parse safeHref decides on, not necessarily the browser's host. On an HTTP dashboard this is a same-scheme relative reference and resolves to the dashboard's own host (measured at a JSDOM anchor); on an HTTPS dashboard it resolves to example.com. No scheme escalation either way.

cases.name: opaque no slash
cases.note: Client is MORE permissive: same as "single slash host" with no slash at all -- WHATWG's new URL() yields host "example.com", net/url yields Host == "". BASE-DEPENDENT for the same reason: on an HTTP dashboard the browser resolves it to the dashboard's own host, not to example.com (measured at a JSDOM anchor).

cases.name: bare space in path
cases.note: Client is MORE permissive: the server's control-character pre-check rejects it (space <= ' ') before net/url is ever consulted, while WHATWG percent-encodes the space to /a%20b and accepts. Not base-dependent: the input carries its own authority, so the host is example.com under either document base.

cases.name: trailing newline
cases.note: Client is MORE permissive: the server's control-character pre-check rejects the trailing \n outright, and net/url would too; WHATWG strips ASCII newlines before parsing, so new URL() sees a clean URL. Not base-dependent: the input carries its own authority.

cases.name: bad percent escape
cases.note: Client is MORE permissive: net/url errors on an invalid escape sequence, while WHATWG's new URL() leaves %zz alone and accepts. Not base-dependent: the input carries its own authority.

cases.name: out of range port
cases.note: Server is MORE permissive here, which is the minority direction: net/url does not range-check the port at Parse time, while WHATWG requires it to be <= 65535 and new URL() throws above that. Not base-dependent: the client rejects it, so nothing reaches a sink to be resolved.

cases.name: empty host with path
cases.note: Client is MORE permissive: WHATWG collapses the empty authority and promotes the first path segment to the host, so new URL("https:///x").hostname === "x"; net/url yields Host == "" and the server rejects. Not base-dependent -- measured host "x" under both an http and an https document base.
